He encouraged the graduates to be confident in their blackness and to expand their moral imaginations to understand and empathize with struggles that are different from their own. Obama also stressed the importance of voting and participating in the political process to bring about structural change.

The Obama Administration has refused to grant a waiver for the Jones Act, a 1920 law requiring that all cargo and passengers moving between points in the United States be transported on American vessels, which would have allowed New Jersey to quickly access tons of salt for ice-covered roads from a port in Maine. The state is currently facing dangerously low levels of salt due to numerous winter storms this year, leaving roadways slick and icy. New Jersey Department of Transportation Spokesman Joe Dee confirmed that a waiver from the Jones Act appears "unlikely." The state is now scrambling to access rock salt, making multiple trips to transport the salt from Maine to New Jersey, which will take a longer time compared to a single trip with a waiver. The numerous winter storms this year have left New Jersey low on salt to treat their roads, and the state may only last through two more snowfalls with the current supply. The salt shortage has made it impossible for municipalities to share salt as they have done in the past. The Obama Administration came under fire for not granting a waiver during the Gulf Oil spill, but they did grant a waiver after Gov. Andrew Cuomo (D., N.Y.) requested one to allow fuel supplies to be replenished in the wake of Hurricane Sandy in 2012.

The bomb that exploded in Manhattan, New York City on September 17th was found to contain residue of Tannerite, a legal product primarily used for target practice. Tannerite is a binary explosive, meaning it is sold in two inert pieces that are not explosive until mixed. When mixed, Tannerite explodes when struck by a bullet from a high-powered rifle. The bombing injured 29 people.

The ATF does not regulate the sale and distribution of the two chemicals used in Tannerite, even when sold together in binary "kits." However, mixing binary components together constitutes manufacturing explosives, and the ATF warns that these products are "high explosives and should be treated with caution and in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions."

After a failed attempt last year, Indiana state senator Jim Merritt will again introduce a bill in January 2017 that would prohibit the sale of Tannerite to customers younger than 18 and also require retailers to place the products behind the counter or in a locked display case.

The company that makes Tannerite is skeptical about reports that their product was used in the bombing, as Tannerite can only be detonated by the impact of a high-velocity bullet, and there have been no reports that a gunshot was used to trigger the bomb. The company is working to determine whether their product was definitely used in the bombing.

The suspect in the bombings, Ahmad Khan Rahami, will be charged with five counts of attempted murder. The investigation is ongoing.

On January 2, 1988, a newborn boy was found dead in Meriden, Connecticut, wrapped in a blanket near a tree. The baby was full-term, blond, and blue-eyed, and the former Chief Robert E. Kosienski said he would have gladly adopted him into his family. The police never found his mother or identified him, and no one was charged in his death. Every year since 1988, the Meriden Police Department and a local church have gathered to pay their respects and remember David Paul.

The tragic event led to the state making it clear that new mothers can go to any hospital and they will take care of the baby no questions asked. This year, the memorial service held at Walnut Grove Cemetery was particularly poignant, as it came just over a year since the tragedy at Sandy Hook Elementary. The service was attended by about 20 members of the Meriden police department and the Rev. Alden Barnes, pastor of First United Methodist Church. Barnes read a prayer for children, keeping in mind the recent one-year anniversary of the Sandy Hook tragedy. The memorial service served as a reminder of the vulnerability of children in society and the commitment of the police department to protect them.

Dave Mirra, a BMX icon and the first action sports athlete to be diagnosed with chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), suffered from the neurodegenerative disease that has been linked to repeated head trauma. The diagnosis was confirmed by multiple neuropathologists, including Dr. Lili-Naz Hazrati from the University of Toronto. Mirra died in February at the age of 41 from a self-inflicted gunshot wound.

The tau protein deposits found in Mirra's brain were similar to those found in the brains of former football and hockey players with CTE. Mirra's widow, Lauren, spoke about his diagnosis, his last weeks, and his legacy in an exclusive interview with ESPN The Magazine. She mentioned that Mirra had suffered a fractured skull when a car hit him at age 19 and endured countless concussions during his BMX career, beginning at a young age.

Mirra was a legend in freestyle BMX and was the face of his sport to the mainstream. He owned the record for the most X Games medals in history with 24 and had a successful video game series and hosted a show on MTV. After retiring from competitive BMX in 2011, Mirra competed in the sports of rallycross and triathlon.

After his death, Mirra's family decided to have his brain studied for CTE. The diagnosis was confirmed by additional U.S. and Canadian neuropathologists who reviewed Hazrati's slides without background information or Mirra's name attached.

CTE is a progressive disease associated with repeated head trauma and was not discovered in football players and other athletes until 2002. Mirra will be inducted into the National BMX Hall of Fame on June 11 and will be honored June 4 during this year's X Games in Austin, Texas, with a new event named for him, the Dave Mirra BMX Park Best Trick competition.

Mirra's widow, Lauren, received the diagnosis about her late husband in March. She spoke about the personality changes she noticed in his final year and expressed hope that the diagnosis would bring awareness to CTE and help in the development of tests to diagnose it in the living. CTE can only be diagnosed after death, though many researchers are working on tests to diagnose it in the living.

In addition to Mirra, another group of researchers announced that former All-Pro defensive end Bubba Smith was the 90th former NFL player diagnosed with CTE on the same day. The diagnosis of CTE in action sports athletes like Mirra and Smith highlights the need for further research and awareness of the risks associated with repeated head trauma in sports.
