In response, activist Charlotte Laws plans to file the Intolerant Jackass Act, which would require anyone proposing such a hateful initiative to attend sensitivity training and donate to pro-gay organizations. The California Bar Association is being urged to disbar McLaughlin due to his advocacy for murder, and state Sen. Ricardo Lara has asked for an investigation. The Sodomite Suppression Act has sparked outrage and calls for action to prevent it from becoming law.

The Sandra Bullock and George Clooney-starring space drama "Gravity" soared to the top of the box office during its opening weekend, earning $55.55 million, marking the biggest October debut ever. The film, directed by Alfonso Cuarón, features groundbreaking visual effects and explores the challenges faced by two astronauts during a spacewalk. The film's success is attributed to its strong performance in 3-D, which accounted for roughly 80% of weekend business. Meanwhile, "Runner Runner," the only other film that debuted nationwide this weekend, fell short of expectations with a disappointing $7.6-million start. "Gravity" has been praised by critics and audiences alike, with a 98% fresh rating on Rotten Tomatoes and an average grade of A- from moviegoers. The film was co-financed by Warner Bros. and Brett Ratner's RatPac-Dune Entertainment for $110 million. "Gravity" will open in Brazil, South Korea, and Mexico later this month. "Runner Runner," which cost $30 million to produce, failed to connect with a younger audience and received negative reviews. The film stars Ben Affleck and Justin Timberlake and tells the story of a grad student who travels to Costa Rica to meet up with a seedy online gambling magnate. The film opened in third place and received an average grade of C from moviegoers.

The United Kingdom's general election on June 8, 2017, resulted in a hung parliament, with no party winning an outright majority. The Conservative Party, led by Prime Minister Theresa May, won 318 seats, while Labour, led by Jeremy Corbyn, won 262 seats. This is eight seats short of a majority for the Conservatives.

Theresa May has stated that her party has the "legitimacy" to govern, and plans to form a minority government, relying on the support of the Democratic Unionist Party (DUP) from Northern Ireland. The DUP has 10 seats in the House of Commons.

If the Conservatives and DUP form an alliance, they would together have more than the 326 seats required for a majority to pass a legislative programme. Negotiations are currently underway between the two parties.

In theory, if the Conservatives fail to secure DUP backing, Labour could attempt to form its own minority government. However, this is unlikely, as Labour has ruled out a coalition.

A minority government means that the Conservatives will fill all the ministerial positions themselves, but will rely on the support of the DUP to help them pass legislation. The key to this is an arrangement called "confidence and supply," whereby the DUP would support the Tories if a vote of no confidence was called and help them to pass their Budget. Negotiations would still be needed to prevent ordinary day-to-day government business from being defeated.

The Brexit negotiations are due to begin on June 19, and the EU has warned that time is running out. If it takes a while to form a government, the UK could ask the EU for a delay.

The first deadline for the new government to be finalized is Tuesday, June 13, when the new Parliament meets for the first time. Theresa May has until this date to put together a deal to keep herself in power or resign, according to official guidance issued by the Cabinet Office. She is entitled to wait until the new Parliament to see if she has the confidence of the House of Commons.

The government then needs to see if it can assemble the votes it needs to get its programme of proposed new laws passed in the Queen's Speech, which is scheduled for Monday, June 19. This is when it will be relying on the DUP's support.

A coalition is unlikely, as Labour has ruled one out, and an alliance with the Liberal Democrats, SNP, Plaid Cymru, and Greens would still leave Labour short of a majority.

Several elections in the early part of the 20th century resulted in minority government, and governments have also started out with majorities which were then lost due to by-elections and defections. Labour had a majority of three after the 1974 general election but this had vanished by 1977, and it stayed in power thanks to a "pact" with the Liberal Party. And John Major's Conservative government started out with a majority of 21 in 1992 but was a minority government by the 1997 general election.

A Cambria County woman, Theresa Plummer, is believed to have died last week as a result of coming into contact with drug paraphernalia while cleaning up her son's suspected overdose scene. According to the coroner, she may have absorbed a substance through her skin or had a reaction after handling the paraphernalia. Theresa Plummer stayed at her son's bedside in intensive care last week as doctors treated him for a suspected overdose. She found her son, Ronald, passed out in the bathroom of his home and went back to clean up. Autopsies have been performed, but toxicology reports are still pending. The coroner advises extreme caution when coming into contact with any powder substance and recommends notifying the proper authorities. The authorities couldn't immediately identify the drugs involved in the case, and toxicology results for the Plummers won't be back for another six to eight weeks.

The European Space Agency's (ESA) Schiaparelli probe, part of the ExoMars program, is believed to have crashed on Mars on October 19th. This conclusion is based on images taken by NASA's Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO) which show a dark patch and a white spot in the targeted landing zone, consistent with a high-velocity impact and the probe's parachute respectively. The probe's descent systems are thought to have malfunctioned, with the parachute jettisoned too early and the retrorockets firing for only a few seconds instead of the required half a minute.

The MRO imagery is not definitive due to its low resolution, but the context is persuasive. The dark patch, about 15m by 40m, is located about 5.5km west of the expected touchdown point in the equatorial Meridiani Plain and is not present in previous MRO pictures of the location. The white blob, which resembles Schiaparelli's 15m-wide parachute, is 1km to the south of the patch and was not present in earlier pictures.

ESA and Nasa are confident that these features represent the scene of Schiaparelli's contact with the surface. Engineers are analyzing the telemetry the probe transmitted during its descent to establish why the parachute and rocket thrusters behaved the way they did, and to identify the height above the surface that each event occurred. The investigation should reveal at what stage in the descent sequence Schiaparelli went into freefall and the speed with which it smacked into the ground, estimated to be greater than 300km/h.

Further photographic insights will come from MRO next week when it flies back over the scene with its high-resolution (HiRISE) camera, capable of distinguishing objects on the ground a mere 30cm to 60cm across. Schiaparelli was a technology demonstrator for Europe's future Mars missions, including the landing of a six-wheeled rover in 2021. Despite the crash, ESA director-general, Jan Woerner, stated that Schiaparelli returned 80% of its anticipated descent telemetry, making it a success in terms of the data it provided for future missions.

In the tiny Pacific nation of Palau, six bodies believed to be Japanese soldiers who fought in World War II have been discovered in a reopened cave, sealed off for nearly 70 years. The cave is located on the island of Pelileu, one of around 200 sealed caves on the island, which were used during a fierce battle between US and Japanese forces in September 1944.

Steve Ballinger, operations director with non-government organisation Cleared Ground Demining, stated that the bodies would be repatriated, and other war relics were also found in and around the cave. The decision to open the caves in Palau comes ahead of an imperial visit next week by Japanese emperor Akihito and empress Michiko.

The team tasked with making the caves safe for anthropologists to investigate has been operating in Palau for six years, clearing remnants of WWII ordnance. The team, made up of 18 Palauans, two Britons, one person each from South Africa and Australia, had concerns about possible booby traps when they first entered the cave.

An estimated 10,000 Japanese soldiers died during the fighting in Palau, and the remains of some 2,600 troops have never been found. The search for the bodies has also focused on a long-lost mass grave on the western side of the island, close to where the current cave search is being conducted. US military documents indicating the cemetery's location were found two years ago at a naval museum in California.

The attempt to find the bodies has been welcomed in Japan and is part of an effort to end a brutal chapter from the war, in which US marines were pitted against Japanese troops who had set up their defences in the intricate labyrinth of heavily fortified caves and underground bunkers. It is still regarded as one of the harshest conflicts in the history of the marines. Unlike previous battles in the Pacific, the Japanese did not focus their defence on using suicide charges to prevent the Americans from establishing a beachhead. Instead, the Japanese forces largely allowed the marines to land but staged their defence from inside the caves. The Japanese, who had occupied Palau for about 30 years, had spent decades using dynamite and axes to enlarge existing caves on Peleliu and blast out new ones. The caves and their entrances were then heavily camouflaged.

In a tragic double shooting on Saturday, 18-year-old Mary Kristene Chapa was shot in the head and is making an "amazing" recovery, while her girlfriend, 19-year-old Mollie Judith Olgin, was killed. The incident occurred at Andrews Park in Portland, Texas. The Portland police chief has stated that while it has been confirmed that the two victims were in a same-sex relationship, there is currently no evidence to suggest the attacks were a hate crime. The Texas Rangers have joined the investigation.

Chapa's brother, Hilario Chapa, shared that his sister took sign language in high school and has been able to communicate in that way during her recovery. She has made physical progress on her right side but is still waiting for a response from the left side of her body. The doctors are optimistic about her progress, and no one has used the word "paralyzed" yet.

The Chapa family, who are Mexican-American and live in Sinton, Texas, have set up an official donation page on WePay to help pay for Chapa's medical bills. The family of Mollie Olgin has reached out to meet with the Chapa family, but the meeting has not yet taken place due to Chapa's mother's emotional state.

The shooting has received widespread support from across the country, with a Facebook event for a "candle lit walk in memory of Olgin and to keep Kristene Chapa in prayers for a speedy recovery" attracting 741 participants. The family has also expressed gratitude for the support they have received from the gay community.

Mario Olgin, Mollie's father, has expressed confidence that justice will be served for his daughter's death. A memorial service for Olgin will be held on Friday, followed by a candlelight vigil at the Violet Andrews Park. The investigation into the double shooting is ongoing.

The article discusses the societal pressure and misconceptions surrounding gender identity and sexuality, particularly in children. It begins with a mother's concern that her son's preference for feminine activities might indicate he will grow up to be gay. The author argues that this conflation of gender expression and sexuality is common and problematic, as it can lead to unnecessary judgments and bullying.

The article cites examples of famous personalities, including Dr. Phil and a blogger named Nerdy Apple Bottom, who have faced backlash for their children's gender-nonconforming behavior. It also mentions the historical blame of mothers for their children's challenges, such as autism and schizophrenia.

The author criticizes Dr. Phil for his contradictory advice, as he acknowledges that homosexuality is not a choice but encourages parents to discourage their children from expressing feminine behaviors. The article ends with a call for society to accept and support children's gender identity, rather than imposing societal norms and expectations on them.

Additionally, the article mentions a political scandal involving a 28-year-old woman named Krystal Ball, who is running for Congress from Virginia. She has been criticized for explicit photos that surfaced online, but she claims it is sexist to post them. The article also includes a satirical section about a home invasion drill and a local politician's financial troubles.

On June 26, 2018, a disgruntled Air Force veteran identified as John Michael Watts, aged 58, set himself on fire outside the Georgia State Capitol in Atlanta as a protest against the Department of Veterans Affairs. Watts, who has no current address, was taken to Grady Memorial Hospital with burns covering 85 to 90 percent of his body.

The incident caused the evacuation of the Capitol and judiciary buildings, and nearby buildings were also evacuated as a precaution. Watts was reportedly strapped with homemade incendiary devices and firecrackers, and doused himself with a flammable liquid before igniting the fireworks.

Several loud explosions were heard, and a trooper quickly put out the fire with an extinguisher. No other injuries were reported. The area was secured by multiple agencies, including the GBI and bomb techs, who examined the contents of Watts' car.

The incident occurred during a news conference about a new state law on hands-free driving. Watts reportedly indicated that he was disgruntled with the V.A. system and was seeking attention for that. The authorities shut down the area around the Capitol and called the bomb squad to ensure that Watts' vehicle did not contain explosives. All roads in the area were reopened by 6:15 p.m. on the same day.

In the lead-up to the new year, two young Tibetan monks, Kelsang and Kunchak, set themselves on fire in a protest against Chinese government religious controls in western China. The incident occurred at the Kirti monastery, a site of frequent protests against Chinese policies. The monks suffered slight burns and were reported to be in stable condition by Chinese state news agency Xinhua. The self-immolations come six months after another monk from the same monastery burned himself to death.

China's stance on the Dalai Lama's succession was also highlighted in the news. The Dalai Lama announced that he would decide on his reincarnation when he is "about 90," contradicting China's claim that the title of Dalai Lama is conferred by the central government. China's foreign ministry stated that any reincarnation process must follow the country's laws and regulations, and the Dalai Lama choosing his own successor is not the traditional practice.

The self-immolations and the Dalai Lama's announcement on his succession have the potential to escalate tensions in the region, with the possibility of two Dalai Lamas being recognized – one by China and the other by exiles or with the blessing of the current Dalai Lama. This situation echoes the 1995 incident where China rejected the Dalai Lama's choice for the next Panchen Lama, leading to the appointment of a Chinese-raised Panchen Lama who supports Beijing's rule over Tibet. The Dalai Lama fled Tibet following a failed uprising against Chinese rule in 1959 and later founded the government in exile in Dharamshala, India. China vilifies him as a "separatist" who incites violence in Tibet, while he insists his focus is on a peaceful campaign for greater autonomy for his homeland.

In a tragic incident, a shooting at Azana Salon & Spa in Brookfield, Wisconsin, left at least three people dead and four injured. The suspected gunman, Radcliffe F. Haughton, is being sought by authorities. The victims were reportedly employees of the spa, and Haughton's estranged wife, Zina Haughton, was among them. Zina was a popular hair stylist who was well-liked by her customers, often remembering their children's names and talking about her two daughters. Haughton's customers described her as a warm, loving person who was dedicated to her family.

Authorities believe the shooting was related to a domestic dispute. Haughton had reported tire slashing and obtained a temporary restraining order against him in October. A four-year restraining order was issued by a Milwaukee County court last week. The names of the deceased and injured have not been released, but it is confirmed that Haughton's two daughters are safe.

Witnesses reported that Haughton, who was called "Rad" by his estranged wife, entered the salon and went past the receptionist. One victim heard shooting a short time later and managed to escape by finding an open door and rolling down a hill towards police. The four wounded were being treated at Froedtert Hospital in Wauwatosa, and all were expected to survive.

Governor Scott Walker, President Barack Obama, and U.S. Rep. Paul Ryan issued statements of condolences. The incident has left Zina Haughton's customers wondering why her husband could commit such a horrible, senseless act. The suspect, Radcliffe Franklin Haughton, was found dead later in the day. The shooting is the second mass shooting in Wisconsin this year.

Sundar Pichai, CEO of Google's main business under Alphabet Inc., received an equity award valued at nearly $200 million, making him one of the world's highest-paid executives. The award, granted on Feb. 3, consists of 273,328 Class C Google stock units that vest in quarterly increments over the next four years, provided Pichai remains employed by Alphabet. The new award lifts the value of Pichai's equity stake in Alphabet to more than $600 million, although it is still less than the stakes held by co-founders Larry Page and Sergey Brin, and Eric Schmidt, Alphabet’s executive chairman. The award is one of the largest by a U.S. company, surpassing the $376 million grant Tim Cook received from Apple Inc. in 2011. Pichai's award is worth more than the $187 million Google agreed to pay the UK government in back taxes since 2005, and he celebrated the award by watching the Super Bowl and meeting NFL legend Ronnie Lott. Other executives, such as Ruth Porat, Alphabet’s chief financial officer, and Diane Greene, head of Google’s cloud computing business, also received significant paydays.

On Thursday, Garry Cordell, one of the men involved in the Schoolcraft County triple homicide case, was sentenced to life in prison without parole. The victims were Jody Hutchinson, Carrie Nelson, and Heather Aldrich. Their bodies were discovered in a burned car in Doyle Township in April. Cordell pleaded guilty to two counts of murder in the first degree and one count of felony murder last week.

At the sentencing, family members of the victims spoke, asking for the maximum sentence. Kim Morrison, aunt of Carrie and Heather, asked Cordell, "How much compassion did you have when you murdered Carrie, Heather, and Jody?" Linda Cole, Jody's mother, said, "You gave my son, my children's brother and my grandchildren's father no mercy, I beg the court to give you none."

Kenneth Brunke, the second suspect, pleaded guilty in October to obstruction of justice and lying to a police officer in exchange for his testimony against Cordell and the late Marietta Carlson. Cordell initially said Brunke helped kill two of the victims in the basement, but later changed his story and said Brunke was not at home when the killings occurred, and that he, Cordell, killed them with the help of Carlson.

Cordell spoke up at the sentencing, saying, "I didn't do this to hurt their family; no way ever will I ask for forgiveness. I'm proud of who I am and what I did and what I stand for." The prosecuting attorney shared a video with photographs of the victims and the burned car, lasting four minutes, which is how long research shows it takes to strangle someone like Cordell did three times.

Judge William Carmody shared that he's never been an advocate of the death sentence, but in this particular instance, he would probably find an exception if this were a different state. "We are happy today even though we have tears in our eyes that justice has been done with Mr. Cordell, and hopefully the same can happen to Mr. Brunke," said Kellie Roll, mother of Carrie and Heather.

Kenneth Brunke will be sentenced on December 10th in Schoolcraft County Circuit Court. The bodies of the victims were discovered in a burned car in Doyle Township in April. The killings horrified residents in this remote, pristine community on the shores of Lake Michigan in the Upper Peninsula. The case seemed solid with police having confessions from two of the suspects, who both named the third as the mastermind behind the killings. However, within months, the story of what happened that April night took a dramatic turn after one of the suspects died in jail, and a new confession emerged. A young, inexperienced prosecutor faced allegations that he mishandled the case after he cut a plea deal with one of the remaining defendants, a move that outraged the victims' families.

The case was about drugs, sex, and betrayal. Kenneth Brunke was a loner, divorced, with a history of depression and suicide threats, when he moved to Manistique from Illinois sometime in 2011. He lived alone in a large, rambling tri-level home on rural Kendall Road and worked as a seasonal employee for the Schoolcraft Road Commission. His real money came from drug sales, with Brunke operating a narcotics ring that supplied local residents with cocaine and morphine.

Heather Aldrich, 25, was vivacious and pretty, a woman who had not lost her looks, despite 10 years of drug addiction. She had a long history of drug abuse. Two months before her murder, she was arrested in a drug and prostitution ring in Gould City. She had a prior drug arrest in 2011 in Newberry. The world's most well-preserved dodo, known as the Oxford Dodo, which inspired Lewis Carroll's Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, met a violent and untimely end, according to new research. The Oxford University Museum of Natural History in the U.K. houses the last remains of a dodo in the world, which includes the mummified bird's skull, foot, and even skin and soft tissue. Using 21st-century forensic scanning technology, researchers have discovered that the Oxford Dodo was shot in the back of the head with a shotgun, making it the first example of lead shots ever used to hunt game birds.

Researchers at the University of Warwick scanned the remains of the dodo using a high-resolution CT scan and software that created a 3D replica of the dodo's skull. They found that the skull contained metallic particles identified as ammunition, indicating that the dodo was hunted down and killed. The researchers are hoping to do a chemical analysis of the lead pellets to trace their origin and potentially determine who killed the dodo.

The Oxford Dodo was always thought to have died of natural causes, but now researchers have proof that it was hunted down and killed. The discovery is a shock and sadness for researchers, as the dodo was extinct just 60 years after it was discovered, in the blink of an eye. The dodo is a symbol of the terrible impact humanity can have on the environment, as they were hunted to extinction by early European explorers and invasive species of animals.

The Royal Ontario Museum in Toronto is the only museum in Canada that has a dodo skeletal display. It's been part of the museum's collection since 1938 and on display for the past 10 years. The murderer of the Oxford Dodo could have been anyone, but the researchers suspect it was either shot in its habitat or kept captive on a ship and shot for food. The researchers are dismayed by this latest discovery about the demise of the dodo, a flightless bird labeled as clumsy and dull-witted.

The Wind River Earthquake, which struck Wyoming in 2013, is considered one of the deepest earthquakes ever recorded, according to a new study published in Earth and Planetary Science Letters. The earthquake, with a magnitude of 4.7 Mw, occurred unusually deep within the Earth's mantle, approximately 75 km, making it among the three deepest earthquakes recorded in a region covered by a stable continental crust.

The Wind River area is seismically quiet, with few earthquakes recorded in the past 60 years, and the nearest tectonic movement occurring 200 km away at the Yellowstone Hotspot. The extreme depth of the Wind River Earthquake poses some interesting questions, as earthquakes usually occur along fault lines in the Earth's crust or as slabs of crust descend deeper into the Earth's mantle.

The scientists suggest that the Wind River earthquake occurred deeper within the Earth's mantle rather than within the Earth's crust. This could mean that the mantle is brittle under the Wind River Craton, and it failed, producing the shock. However, this finding does not match our current understanding of the forces needed to deform and break the mantle in such areas, leaving the true cause of the quake open to debate.

The study sheds light on the deep seismic activity that can occur in volcanic regions but is usually at a much smaller magnitude. The Wind River location is not near any active surface volcanoes and is unlikely to be connected to the volcanic region 200 km away at the Yellowstone Hotspot. The size and type of shock produced by the Wind River earthquake suggest it was produced by tectonic forces, rather than by the movement of magma or fluid in the Earth's mantle.

The Wind River Earthquake is a significant finding as it challenges our understanding of the Earth's mantle and the forces that can cause earthquakes. Further research is needed to understand the true cause of the quake and the properties of the Earth's mantle in the Wind River Craton.

The article discusses the importance of nutrition for astronauts during long-duration spaceflights, specifically focusing on the research conducted by NASA's Nutritional Biochemistry Lab. The lab's manager, Scott M. Smith, explains that proper nutrition is crucial for the success of space missions, as a lack of it can lead to various health issues such as bone and muscle loss, cardiovascular degradation, and impairment of the immune system.

Astronauts tend to eat less in space due to being busy and experiencing menu fatigue. Additionally, the space environment presents unique challenges to maintaining a healthy diet, including microgravity, higher radiation exposure, and changes in temperature and humidity. To counteract these effects, Smith and his team are working to understand the body's requirements for nutrients, ensure that the food system has those nutrients, and that they are stable over the duration of a long spaceflight.

To assess the impact of spaceflight on nutrition, astronauts provide blood and urine samples before, during, and after their missions. A biochemical profile is created for each astronaut, and the ultimate goal is to keep astronauts healthy from a nutrition perspective while they are on the mission. The Biochemical Profile project examines nutritional markers such as proteins, vitamins, minerals, bone markers, hormones, metabolites, immune function, antioxidants, and general chemistry to better understand these changes.

The Twins Study, which involves astronaut Scott Kelly and his twin brother Mark, brings a unique element to this investigation. Scott Kelly is currently on a one-year mission aboard the International Space Station, while Mark remains on Earth. The tracking of Scott's overall nutritional status during flight as compared to Mark's on Earth is of particular interest to these investigators.

The article also provides a historical context by discussing scurvy, a disease that plagued sailors centuries ago due to a lack of Vitamin C. The article mentions that between 1500 and 1800, an estimated two million sailors died from scurvy, making it a more significant cause of death than storms, shipwrecks, combat, and all other diseases combined. The article concludes by emphasizing the importance of nutrition for both astronauts and people on Earth, and the ongoing efforts to improve nutritional health on space missions.

He has had deep experience in setting up jihadist groups and organized the flow of fighters from Syria and elsewhere into Iraq, strengthening Al Qaeda in Iraq.

The merger between Al Qaeda in Iraq and al-Nusra will likely increase tensions along the border between Lebanon and Syria, as al-Nusra fighters have been moving into Shiite villages on the Syrian side of the border. The likelihood of a confrontation between Hezbollah and Sunni jihadists has increased, according to Lebanese intelligence sources.

The merger also raises concerns about the future of Syria and the region, as Al Qaeda's ambitions to use the Syrian conflict for greater regional goals are highlighted by the name change to Islamic State of Iraq and Al-Sham. The name refers to Greater Syria, a pan-Arab geographical definition of a hypothetical united Arab state that corresponds to a medieval Arab province encompassing the eastern Mediterranean Sea, the Levant, and Western Mesopotamia.

In recent weeks, al-Nusra fighters have come closer to Lebanon, and there is a risk of a confrontation along the border between Lebanon's Shiite armed movement Hezbollah and Sunni jihadists with al-Nusra. The merger between Al Qaeda in Iraq and al-Nusra will likely further complicate the battlefield, where Western powers have been covertly trying to funnel weapons, training, and aid toward more secular rebel groups and army defectors.

The Obama administration has been right to move deliberately on aid to rebels, as there are unintended consequences and risks in supporting the Syrian opposition, which is fractured into hundreds of local groups, some elements of which are hardly supportive of the United States. The merger between Al Qaeda in Iraq and al-Nusra underscores the need for caution and careful consideration in providing aid to the Syrian opposition.

Gold has since done over 40 interviews with major outlets such as CNN, Good Morning America, and Marketplace. The policy has received positive feedback from other restaurant owners worldwide. However, Gold mentioned that the policy has not significantly increased business yet, but he expects an increase once schools reopen. The policy aims to create a more intimate dining experience and has been well-received by customers, with almost half taking advantage of the offer. The policy serves as a reminder for Gold to limit his own cell phone usage during meals as well.

The U.S. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has imposed a 24-hour restriction on flights to Tel Aviv, Israel, following a Hamas rocket explosion near Ben Gurion International Airport. This has led to the cancellation of flights by Air France, Lufthansa, and Air Berlin, with Lufthansa extending the cancelations through Thursday. The European Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) has also recommended that airlines refrain from operating flights to and from Tel Aviv. Other airlines such as KLM, Alitalia, and Scandinavian Airlines have also canceled flights. However, British Airways has not canceled any of its Tel Aviv flights. The FAA is working closely with the Israeli government to review the situation and determine whether potential risks to U.S. civil aviation are mitigated. Critics have lashed out against the FAA's decision, with former New York mayor Michael Bloomberg calling it a "mistake" and praising Tel Aviv Ben Gurion International Airport as the most secure airport on Earth. The Israeli government has assured that the airport is safe from any rocket attack by militants in Gaza. The FAA's decision has caused disruptions for travelers and stranded some in Tel Aviv. The closure is a significant blow to Israel's economy, particularly its tourism industry, which received a record 3.5 million visitors in 2013.

The New York Jets have reached a $325,000 settlement with their cheerleading squad, the Flight Crew, in a class-action lawsuit filed in 2014. The lawsuit, led by cheerleader Krystal C., alleged that the cheerleaders were paid only $150 per game and nothing for practice time, resulting in hourly wages below minimum wage.

The settlement will provide each cheerleader with $2,500 for each season they worked during the 2012-13 and 2013-14 NFL seasons. Cheerleaders who participated in photo shoots will receive an additional $400 per shoot. The final amount will include interest and will vary based on the number of football seasons each cheerleader worked.

This isn't the first time an NFL team has faced a wage lawsuit from its cheerleaders. Similar lawsuits have been filed against the Cincinnati Bengals, Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Oakland Raiders, and Buffalo Bills. The Buccaneers reached a settlement of $825,000, the Bengals have tentatively agreed to a pact with their cheerleaders, and the Raiders settled for $1.25 million in 2014. The Buffalo Jills, the cheerleaders for the Buffalo Bills, were recently granted class-action status in a similar wage suit against their team.

State Senator Diane Savino (D-SI) has called on the NFL to establish uniform rules for its teams to ensure fair pay and treatment for all cheerleaders. She also urged the Buffalo Bills to follow the Jets' example and settle the lawsuit with their cheerleaders.

Christopher Driskill, a married doctor and the president-elect of the New Mexico Medical Society, is under investigation for multiple allegations of misconduct. The New Mexico Medical Board has suspended Driskill's license, citing incidents where he allegedly kept a stash of alcohol at work, drank on the job, and worked under the influence. Driskill is also accused of having sexual relationships with patients and employees, leaving women to give birth unattended, and writing lewd notes on medical charts.

One particularly concerning incident involved Driskill leaving a woman in labor alone because he was having sex with another patient. The board's report, shared by the Albuquerque Journal, states that Driskill posed a 'clear and immediate danger to the public' due to his multiple infractions.

Driskill was fired from his job at Premier Health in Hobbs in August and failed to inform the board about his termination and subsequent leave of absence. He has not yet requested a hearing to appeal the suspension of his license. The New Mexico Medical Society, which represents the majority of physicians in New Mexico, has not yet commented on the matter.

The allegations against Driskill are serious and potentially life-threatening, as they involve neglecting patients during labor and delivering substandard care. The investigation into his conduct is ongoing, and a hearing date has not yet been set to determine whether his license will be revoked.

A New Zealand father, Samuel Forrest, is making headlines after he was abandoned by his Armenian wife following the birth of their son, Leo, who has Down syndrome. Born on January 21, 2023, Leo was initially rejected by his mother due to societal stigma towards children with disabilities in Armenia.

Forrest, who is originally from Auckland, New Zealand, was shocked to learn about the hospital's practices in Armenia regarding children with special needs. His wife had already made arrangements to abandon Leo, and he only found out about it after the birth.

The news of Forrest's plight has sparked an outpouring of support, with a GoFundMe page set up to help him return to New Zealand with Leo. The fundraiser, which initially aimed to raise $10,000, has seen an astonishing increase, reaching over $160,000 in just a few hours.

Forrest plans to move back to New Zealand with Leo, where they will receive support from family and friends. He hopes to secure a part-time job to care for Leo without the need for daycare. He also aims to work with disability awareness groups to educate parents about children with special needs and prevent similar situations from happening.

Forrest remains hopeful and optimistic about Leo's future, describing him as "great" and determined to find his unique niche. He is adamant about challenging societal perceptions and labels surrounding children with Down syndrome, believing they are just as normal as any other child, albeit with some differences.

The baby's mother, Ruzan Badalyan, has declined to comment on the matter. Attempts to reach the hospital for comment were unsuccessful at the time of reporting.

In a twist of events, the online auction for George Zimmerman's gun, which he used to shoot and kill Trayvon Martin, was found to be a fake public auction. The real auction, open only to pre-qualified bidders, was being held privately by United Gun Group. The fake auction, hosted on a different website, had a high bid near $140,000, but the real auction on UnitedGunGroup.com had a winning bid of $120,000 from at least one verified bidder. The identity of the real auction winner remains undisclosed.

Zimmerman, in a statement, thanked God for the successful auction and expressed gratitude to United Gun Group for hosting the auction. He also criticized GunBroker.com and praised the members of United Gun Group for terminating their relationship with the former. Zimmerman stated that the auction with United Gun Group is now closed, and the winning bidder will be notified immediately.

The Trayvon Martin Foundation declined to comment on the sale of the gun. The Kel-Tec PF-9 pistol, which Zimmerman is trying to sell, is the one he used to shoot Martin in 2012 after a confrontation in his Sanford neighborhood. Zimmerman was acquitted by a jury in 2013.

In his post introducing the auction, Zimmerman touted the handgun as "a piece of American history." The gun still carries the case number from his trial in silver permanent marker, as per Zimmerman. The first listing for the gun, posted on a different website last week, prompted worldwide headlines and controversy, resulting in the auction being pulled from the site. The gun was later posted on UnitedGunGroup.com.

The U.S. Supreme Court's decision to legalize gay marriage across the country, including in the 13 states that previously banned it, was met with both celebration and controversy. In response to the backlash, the PennLive newsroom decided to limit op-eds and letters to the editor opposing same-sex marriage, comparing them to racist, sexist, or anti-Semitic speech. However, the move was met with criticism, with many accusing the news organization of censorship and violating the First Amendment. The newsroom's editor-in-chief apologized, stating that the intention was to foster a civil discussion, and that all views are welcome in the pages of PennLive/The Patriot-News.

In other news, Seth Meyers and Amy Poehler teamed up to shame a Sports Illustrated contributor who tweeted that women's sports, not just soccer, aren't worth watching. Wal-Mart is also under fire for refusing to bake a cake with the Confederate battle flag but agreeing to bake a cake with the ISIS battle flag. Takata, the Japanese supplier of airbags, is facing a crisis over deadly defects in its airbags, with at least eight deaths and 130 injuries linked to the problem. The company's reclusive CEO, Shigehisa Takada, has finally addressed the issue, offering an apology but defending Takata's products as safe.

In a separate incident, a man in Slidell, Louisiana, presented a YouTube video showing how Wal-Mart refused to bake a cake with the Confederate battle flag but agreed to bake a cake with the ISIS battle flag. Wal-Mart has since apologized for the mistake.

Finally, Takata's CEO has defended the company's use of ammonium nitrate, a potentially unstable propellant, in its airbags, stating that it is safe and reliable. However, some experts suspect that the basic design of Takata's inflaters is dangerous, and the company is still trying to pinpoint the exact cause of the defects.

Archaeologists have discovered a mysterious enclosure, believed to be a large void, hidden deep inside the Great Pyramid of Giza, the oldest of the seven wonders of the ancient world. The void, which stretches for at least 30 meters and lies above the grand gallery, is the first major structure found in the pyramid since the 19th century. It is unclear whether the void is a chamber or a corridor, or whether it played any more than a structural role in the pyramid's construction.

Scientists discovered the void using sensors that detect particles known as muons, which rain down on Earth when cosmic rays slam into atoms in the upper atmosphere. The muons travel at close to the speed of light and behave much like x-rays when they meet objects. Armed with suitable equipment, researchers can use them to reveal the rough internal structure of pyramids and other ancient monuments.

The Great Pyramid, also known as Khufu's Pyramid or the Pyramid of Cheops, was built in the 4th dynasty by the pharaoh Khufu, who reigned from 2509 to 2483 BC. The monument rises 140 meters above the Giza Plateau and has three chambers known from previous explorations: a subterranean one at the base of the pyramid, the Queen's chamber at the center, and the King's chamber above. While a granite sarcophagus sits in the King's chamber, King Khufu's mummy is missing, and his queens were buried elsewhere. Whatever riches were once in the chambers were looted long ago.

Egyptologists have scores of theories about how the pyramid was built, but there are no reliable accounts of its construction. The mammoth construction project occupied the lives of a hundred thousand men, fuelled in part by radishes, onions, and leeks, according to Herodotus.

To pinpoint the cavity, scientists from Nagoya University in Japan, and KEK, the country's high energy physics lab, installed muon-detecting photographic plates and electronic muon detectors around the Queen's chamber. At the same time, researchers from CEA, France's energy research organization, trained "muon telescopes" on the pyramid from the outside. All three techniques can tell from which direction incoming muons arrive.

When the teams compared their results, all had found a muon hotspot in the same place, indicating the presence of a large cavity in the pyramid. While most of the monument is made of stone that absorbs muons, chambers and cavities let the particles pass through.

Muon analysis allows scientists to look deep inside ancient monuments without drilling holes or causing other damage to the precious structures. But the technique produces low-resolution images, making it impossible for the researchers to tell if the newly-found void runs horizontally or parallel to the grand gallery. Nor can they be sure it is a single enclosure rather than a series of smaller cavities close together.

The team has no plans to drill into the cavity to explore inside, but they are developing a tiny flying robot that might one day be sent in, if the Egyptian authorities approve.

The discovery of the void has deepened the mysteries of the pyramids, and experts are calling for further non-invasive exploration to shed more light on the purpose of the cavity. Some believe it may have relieved weight on the roof of the underlying grand gallery, or be a hitherto unknown corridor in the pyramid. The team is being careful not to describe the cavity as a "chamber," as it may have been incorporated by the builders to avoid collapse by relieving some of the stress of the overlying weight of stone.

The muon science used to discover the void is sound, but some experts are not yet convinced of its significance. They say it could be a space that the builders left to protect the very narrow roof of the Grand Gallery from the weight of the pyramid. Further investigation is needed to determine the true nature and purpose of the void.

The discovery of the void is a tribute to the ingenuity and skill of the ancient Egyptians, who built the pyramids with the means they had 4,000 or 5,000 years ago and left a lasting heritage for future generations. The void asks a question about what is our future, and what will our own society leave for future generations?

On Friday night in Denver, a high-speed chase involving a stolen tractor occurred through central Denver, ending in Lower Downtown. The tractor was initially stolen from a Denver Water facility in the Lincoln Park neighborhood. The chase, which involved multiple Denver Police Department vehicles, resulted in two officers being hospitalized with injuries, both of whom were later treated and released.

Videos captured the pursuit, showing the tractor driving on busy city streets and sidewalks, with one clip showing it crossing Park Avenue. The pursuit ended near 15th and Market Streets in LoDo, when a police cruiser rammed into the tractor, causing the airbags to deploy. The tractor driver was subsequently subdued using a Taser by an officer.

Witnesses reported that the tractor struck several cars and buildings during the chase, and that the officer who rammed their vehicle into the tractor showed remarkable dedication in ending the pursuit. The suspect's identity has not been released as the investigation is ongoing.

Authorities are treating the two injured officers, and further details regarding the circumstances of the chase are expected to be released as the investigation progresses. The public is encouraged to stay updated through the news app for iPhone and Android.

The research conducted by Brigham Young University geologists reveals that the mountains on Oahu, Hawaii are being dissolved by groundwater, leading to the eventual transformation of the island into a flat, low-lying island similar to Midway. This dissolution occurs at a faster rate than the erosion caused by external forces. The study, published in Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, found that groundwater removes more mineral material from the island than stream water. The researchers also noted that Oahu's growth will continue for approximately 1.5 million years, after which the force of groundwater will cause the island to descend into a low-lying topography. The study's findings provide insights into the weathering rates of the Hawaiian Islands, which are all composed of the same volcanic rock and have variable weathering rates due to varying rainfall.

The latest Gallup poll reveals that Congress has reached an all-time low approval rating of 10%, the lowest in the polling organization's nearly 40-year history. This dismal rating places Congress below several unpopular figures, including Fidel Castro, Saddam Hussein, Osama bin Laden, and Mark Fuhrman.

Interestingly, Americans express more favorable views towards several entities than Congress, such as BP during the oil spill, socialism, waterboarding, abortion, President Nixon during the Watergate scandal, Santa Claus, the Prime Minister of Greece, Occupy Wall Street, and even Paris Hilton, the least popular celebrity in an August Ipsos poll.

The low approval rating for Congress reflects the widespread frustration among Americans with their elected officials. This dissatisfaction is further highlighted by the fact that three times as many people have a positive view of socialism than have a positive view of Congress, according to a CBS/New York Times poll.

In a significant development, the Supreme Court appears poised to challenge a key provision of the Voting Rights Act of 1965, potentially allowing nine states, primarily in the South, to alter their voting procedures without federal approval. This decision follows tough questioning from the court's more conservative members during a hearing on February 27, 2013.

The Voting Rights Act, once a landmark civil rights legislation, is under scrutiny due to concerns that it perpetuates racial entitlement, a remark made by Justice Antonin Scalia. This comment sparked a heated exchange, with Justice Sonia Sotomayor questioning whether the right to vote is a racial entitlement.

The conservative wing of the court suggested that the modern South has moved beyond its troubled past, implying that the legal burdens on the nine states are no longer justified. Chief Justice John G. Roberts Jr. and Justice Anthony M. Kennedy raised questions about the continued necessity of the law, with Kennedy asking whether Alabama is an "independent sovereign" or under the "trusteeship of the United States government."

The liberal wing of the court, on the other hand, argued that Congress is entitled to determine that the provision is still needed in the covered jurisdictions. The law, which passed the Senate unanimously and the House overwhelmingly in 2006, is being defended by the NAACP Legal Defense and Educational Fund.

The outcome of the case remains uncertain, but if the court overturns the provision, it could make it easier for lawmakers in the affected states to implement stricter identification standards, move polling places, and redraw legislative districts. The court has suggested that Congress should update its formula to determine which parts of the country should remain subject to the law, a suggestion that Congress has yet to act upon.

The Ig Nobel Prizes, held annually since 1991, honor unusual and imaginative achievements in the fields of science, medicine, and technology that make people laugh and then think. The ceremony takes place at Harvard University's Sanders Theatre, where Nobel laureates hand out the prizes to the winners. The 29th First Annual Ig Nobel Prize ceremony is scheduled for September 12, 2019.

The prizes are organized by the magazine Annals of Improbable Research and co-sponsored by the Harvard-Radcliffe Society of Physics Students and the Harvard-Radcliffe Science Fiction Association. Ten Ig Nobel prizes have been awarded each year since 1991, with a complete list of winners available on the organization's website.

The ceremony is known for its eccentricity, with genuine Nobel laureates handing out the prizes and participating in the event. Delegations of five or more ticket holders can register to be officially celebrated during the event.

The winners are chosen based on whether their research makes people laugh and then think. Many of the studies honored at the ceremony have a humorous or absurd aspect, but they also often tackle real-world problems.

Some examples of past winners include:

* A study of itches by a team of neurologists and psychologists at the University of Lübeck in Germany, in which volunteers were asked to scratch one arm while looking at themselves in a mirror, and reported significant itch relief even when they scratched the wrong arm.
* A study of dragonflies by Gábor Horváth, a biophysicist at Eötvös Loránd University in Budapest, which found that the insects are attracted to black gravestones because they reflect polarized light, leading to the death of many dragonflies.
* A study of horse flies by Horváth, which discovered that white horse fur does not reflect the polarized light that the blood-sucking insects use to find their prey, providing a natural advantage for white horses.
* A study by Charles Foster and Thomas Thwaites, who spent time living as badgers, otters, deer, foxes, and goats to better understand the nonhuman world.

The Ig Nobel Prizes are a lighthearted celebration of the unusual and imaginative aspects of scientific research, and they serve to highlight the importance of curiosity and creativity in the pursuit of knowledge.

The Parsons Green tube bombing occurred on September 15, 2017, in London, England. The bomb, which was partially detonated, injured 29 people, including a young boy. The device was placed in a white plastic bucket inside a Lidl supermarket bag and was believed to have been remotely detonated. Islamic State claimed responsibility for the blast. The UK's terror threat level was raised to critical, indicating a further attack may be imminent. The bomber is still at large, and the investigation is ongoing. The UK government has increased armed police presence on the transport network and in the streets, and military personnel have replaced police officers on guard duties at certain protected sites. The explosion happened at about 8.20am on a District line train at Parsons Green station, and the station has since reopened. The incident is the fifth terrorist attack Britain has suffered in less than six months. The prime minister, Theresa May, condemned the bombing as cowardly, and the home secretary, Amber Rudd, denounced it as "callous and indiscriminate." The London mayor, Sadiq Khan, described the attack as hideous and added: "We will never be defeated." The security minister Ben Wallace told the BBC on Saturday: "We haven't been able at the moment to catch the bomber. The bomber is still out there – or bombers – and we have to get to the bottom of that and follow up the leads." The Met assistant commissioner Mark Rowley, the UK's most senior anti-terror police officer, said police were "chasing down suspects." The investigation is being led by Scotland Yard's counter-terrorism command. The device was packed with chemicals and may offer clues about its construction and the materials used to make the explosive charge. The bomb-making knowledge may have been acquired from DIY guides on the internet or from another person. The explosion at Parsons Green is the first terrorist attack in the UK this year to not result in loss of life. Two vehicle and knife attacks in London and a bombing in Manchester were blamed on Islamist-motivated terrorism, and a van attack in June was blamed on an extreme rightwing motivation. The US president, Donald Trump, tweeted about the attack, but his comments were dismissed as "unhelpful" by a police spokesman. May also criticized Trump, saying: "I never think it is helpful for anybody to speculate on what is an ongoing investigation."

A Facebook campaign to boycott Spirit Airlines has gained significant traction, with over 18,000 likes as of Thursday morning, following the airline's refusal to refund the cost of a dying veteran's flight. Jerry Meekins, a 76-year-old former marine, requested a refund on his $197 flight to New Jersey from Florida, but was denied due to his terminal esophageal cancer. The campaign, initially started in 2010 over the airline's policy of charging for checked luggage, has garnered support from current military members and veterans. One commenter, Robert Twigg, wrote, "I believe Spirit Airlines owes a debt to the Veteran and an apology."

In addition to the Facebook campaign, the Veterans of the Vietnam War and the Veterans Coalition wrote a letter to Spirit Airlines on Tuesday. The airline did not respond to a request for comment.

Separately, Spirit Airlines announced new carry-on bag fees, with the cost of storing a carry-on bag in overhead bins at the airport gate set to increase from $45 to $100, starting November 6. The new fees will range from $25 to $100 per carry-on bag, up from $20 to 45. The airline claims the new structure will streamline its bag fees, making them identical for domestic and international travelers.

The question remains as to whether Facebook is the right channel for airline boycotts and if there's a better way to build a strong campaign. The controversy surrounding Spirit Airlines' treatment of a dying veteran has sparked a wave of criticism and calls for boycott, with the airline yet to respond.

In Germany, a refrigerated trailer carrying over 20 tons of chocolate, including Nutella and Kinder Surprise eggs, has been stolen. The confections, worth between €50,000 and €70,000, were taken between Saturday evening and midday on Sunday. The police are investigating the theft, unsure if it was planned or opportunistic, and are also looking into possible links with the theft of an empty trailer in Weimar over the weekend. This isn't the first time chocolate has been the target of theft in Germany; last week, 53g of chocolate was found dumped in Bad Oldesloe. Elsewhere, in Austria, police discovered over 9 tons of stolen garlic hidden in vans crossing the Hungarian border. In the U.S., two members of an alleged Russian crime syndicate were charged with transporting and selling 10,000 pounds of stolen chocolate confections. The German police have urged the public to report any large quantities of chocolate offered via unconventional channels.

On Thursday, an Air Algerie flight carrying 116 passengers, including nearly 50 French nationals, crashed in northern Mali. The flight was en route from Burkina Faso to Algiers when it disappeared from radar an hour after takeoff. The exact cause of the crash is unknown, but it is believed that the plane may have encountered bad weather after the pilot requested a change in direction due to a storm.

The search for the wreckage is ongoing, with French warplanes and UN helicopters scouring the area. However, conflicting accounts have emerged regarding the location of the crash, with Malian President Ibrahim Boubacar Keita stating that wreckage was found in his country's far north, while Burkinabe authorities claim to have found remains in southern Mali.

French President Francois Hollande has cancelled a planned visit to overseas territories and has pledged to use all military means to locate the aircraft. The search is complicated by the vast scale and difficult terrain of Mali, with much of the suspected crash site lying in the hands of Tuareg separatist rebels.

The MD-83 aircraft involved in the crash is part of the McDonnell Douglas MD-80 family of twin-engined jets and has a relatively clean safety record, with five accidents since 1977 causing a total of eight deaths. Swiftair, the private Spanish company that owns the plane, has also had a relatively clean safety record.

The crash is likely to add to concerns over air travel following recent incidents, including the downing of a Malaysia Airlines plane over Ukraine last week and the crash of a TransAsia Airways plane during a thunderstorm on Wednesday. Airlines have temporarily cancelled flights into Tel Aviv due to the conflict in Gaza.

The passenger list for the Air Algerie flight included 27 Burkinabe, 51 French, eight Lebanese, six Algerians, two Luxembourgers, five Canadians, four Germans, one Cameroonian, one Belgian, one Egyptian, one Ukrainian, one Swiss, one Nigerian, and one Malian. The Lebanese Foreign Ministry estimates that at least 20 Lebanese citizens were on the flight, some of whom may have dual nationality.

A fatal shooting occurred at Mississippi State University's Evans Hall residence hall on Saturday night, claiming the life of 21-year-old John Sanderson. Three suspects, described as black males, fled the scene in a blue Crown Victoria and are still at large. Campus police were notified of the incident within a minute and found Sanderson in grave condition. He was transported to the hospital but died shortly after. The university is currently under advisory conditions, with increased security measures in place. Authorities believe this to be an isolated incident and have set up a call center for concerned parents.

In a separate incident, a 19-year-old freshman, Nolan Ryan Henderson III, was shot and killed at an off-campus apartment pool party in Jackson, Mississippi, early Sunday. Governor Phil Bryant expressed his sorrow over the loss of both students and has instructed the state public safety commissioner to assist in the investigations.

Both universities have implemented counseling centers and other resources to help students cope with the tragedies. The Mississippi State University president assured students, parents, faculty, and staff that the campus remains safe.

A 37-year-old man, Jedediah Ezekiel Fulton, was arrested in Sutherlin, Oregon on March 16, 2023, for causing a disturbance at a McDonald's restaurant. Police allege that Fulton became upset when his order for 30 double cheeseburgers was refused, leading him to destroy a banner and attack the restaurant's iconic golden arches. The incident escalated when Fulton grabbed a person's shirt, prompting a witness to pull out a gun to protect the individual. Fulton is currently facing charges of second-degree disorderly conduct, second-degree criminal trespass, second-degree criminal mischief, and harassment. It is unclear if Fulton has secured legal representation.

On May 11, 2015, a burglary suspect was arrested in Antioch, California, after a four-year-old girl led police to him. The homeowner, holding her baby, saw an intruder enter her home through an unlocked door and fled with her baby, leaving her four-year-old daughter behind. Upon arrival, police found the young girl at the top of the stairs but no sign of the intruder. The girl then pointed out the intruder, identified as Demaria Lopez, a 21-year-old transient, who was hiding in her closet. A brief struggle ensued, but Lopez was eventually taken into custody without injury. He was booked on suspicion of burglary and resisting arrest, and there were no injuries to any involved. Anyone with information regarding this case is encouraged to contact the Antioch Police Department.

In a surprise appearance at the White House briefing room on Friday, President Obama shared his thoughts on the acquittal of George Zimmerman in the shooting death of Trayvon Martin, stating that it is important to view the case through the lens of past discrimination. Obama, who last year said the 17-year-old Florida shooting victim could just as easily have been his son, spoke about his own experiences of racial prejudice and the ongoing challenges faced by the African American community.

In an emotional and personal 18-minute speech, Obama discussed his own experiences of being followed in department stores and the fear he has seen in his daughters and their friends. He acknowledged the frustration and pain within the African American community, stating that it is important to recognize that their interpretation of the case is informed by past experiences and a history that does not go away.

Obama also addressed the need for self-reflection, asking Americans to "wring as much bias out of themselves as they can." He spoke about the progress that has been made in race relations, but also acknowledged that the country still has a long way to go.

The president also mentioned that he and his deputies were considering concrete policy options in response to the Zimmerman verdict, such as training state and local law enforcement officials to better deal with issues of racial bias, and exploring whether state laws like "Stand Your Ground" might encourage altercations rather than defuse them.

Obama's remarks were his most extensive on race since the 2008 campaign and were met with relief and satisfaction by black leaders who had been urging him to speak out. However, some critics felt that the president's remarks were too little, too late.

The president also paid tribute to Trayvon's parents, saying that he can only imagine what they are going through and that their strength is remarkable. In a statement, Trayvon's parents said they were deeply honored and moved by Obama's comments, stating that he sees himself in Trayvon and identifies with him.

The president's advisers selected the White House briefing room as the location for his remarks, calculating that it would be less formal than a full-dress speech and would shield him from questions about why he had waited days after the verdict to speak. The advisers said that Obama was anxious to confront the issue of race in a way that he has not since he ran for president in 2008.

The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has proposed new rules to protect the public from the risks associated with indoor tanning, particularly for minors. The proposed regulations would ban children under 18 from using tanning beds and require adult customers to sign a consent form every six months acknowledging the risks. The FDA also plans to make safety improvements for tanning devices, such as adding more prominent warnings, emergency shut-off buttons, and eye safety measures. The proposed rules are intended to reduce skin cancer cases and save lives, as indoor tanning is a known contributor to skin cancer, including its most deadly form, melanoma. The public has 90 days to comment on the new rules.

PBS faced backlash on social media after admitting to using footage of previous years' fireworks in its live "A Capitol Fourth" broadcast on July 4th, 2016. Hundreds of viewers complained on Twitter and Facebook that the fireworks display couldn't be live because the images were in clear weather, while Washington, D.C. was heavily overcast and foggy. About 10 p.m. ET, the show's Facebook and Twitter pages acknowledged that the supposedly "live" show was, in fact, a combination of the best fireworks from this year and previous years. Reaction online was swift and savage, with viewers accusing PBS of using stock video and being dishonest. PBS representatives did not immediately return calls for comment. This incident occurred during a time when the show's host, Tom Bergeron, was preparing for the event and was not concerned about potential rain. Despite the controversy, the annual Independence Day concert and fireworks show was held on the National Mall.

The Metropolitan Police in the UK has announced that they are assessing new information regarding the deaths of Princess Diana and Dodi Al Fayed, who died in a car crash in Paris on August 31, 1997. The police emphasized that this is not a reopening of the investigation, but rather an assessment of the new information's relevance and credibility. The assessment will be conducted by officers from the specialist crime and operations command.

The deaths of Diana and Fayed were previously investigated, and an inquest in 2008 found them to be unlawfully killed, with the driver's reckless speed and drinking, as well as the reckless pursuit of paparazzi, contributing to their deaths. The crash occurred after the couple left the Ritz Hotel and were pursued by paparazzi on motorbikes.

Reports suggest that the new information includes allegations of military involvement and that it was passed to the police by an Army source. However, the police declined to discuss the source of the information they are assessing. There has been no comment from Prince William, Prince Harry, or Clarence House regarding the new information.

Dodi Al Fayed's father, Mohamed Al Fayed, expressed interest in seeing the outcome of the police assessment, stating that he trusts the Met to investigate the information "with vigour." Dai Davies, a former head of royal protection, has stated that the deaths were an accident and that three separate inquiries have come to the same conclusion. The cost of the inquest and the Metropolitan Police investigation totaled £12.5 million.
